$comment: SHARED secret-pattern set for the XENO release publishers.
This is the single, updatable source of truth used by every R2 write path
which scanned a REPO; this set is applied to ARTIFACT BYTES, because the artifact is
Extend it by editing this file, or without touching the repo by pointing
XENO_SECRET_PATTERNS at an extra JSON file with the same shape (it is MERGED, never
replaces — you cannot weaken the built-in set with an env var).
`re` is a JS regex source string, compiled with the flags in `flags` (default 'g').
Keep patterns anchored on a distinctive prefix: entropy-only heuristics produce noise,
and a noisy gate gets disabled, which is how leaks ship.

patterns.name: XENO platform API key
patterns.note: THE 2026-03/07 incident. Platform keys are `xeno-` + 48 hex (src/server/middleware/auth.js). Three extension ZIPs carried a live one to R2.

patterns.name: XENO run-scoped token
patterns.note: Agents-API run tokens accepted by the api.xenostudio.ai gateway.

patterns.name: Google API key
patterns.note: The hardcoded Gemini key found in the frontend bundle was this shape.

patterns.name: GitHub token
patterns.note: release-guide/07-troubleshooting.md §6 — a PAT already leaked once via a git remote.

patterns.name: Resend API key
patterns.note: Exact SHA-256 exemption for a lowercase native symbol embedded byte-for-byte in the official Electron 44 Linux executable; the surrounding binary and executable hash were verified before admission.

patterns.name: rclone R2 credential block
patterns.note: The R2 token is the one credential the whole publish path holds; an rclone.conf must never be packaged.
